question: Can public aggregate measurement evidence provide a defensible external anchor separating urge-generation change from action-control change?
interpretation: Insufficient means insufficient for this latent-mechanism identification use, not invalid for all clinical measurement. No formal GRADE assessment.
disconfirmation: Compatible calibration/invariance evidence plus a defensible identifying restriction and sufficient aggregate uncertainty would permit design preparation.

records.title: The premonitory urge to tic: measurement, characteristics, and correlates in older adolescents and adults
records.population: 122 participants aged 16 or older, original adult-dominant CBIT trial.
records.comparator: Screening versus baseline within two weeks, before randomized treatment.
records.result: Internal consistency alpha=.83; test–retest Pearson r=.79, p<.001; PUTS versus YGTSS Total Tic Score (0–50) r=.32.
records.reliability_type: Pearson test–retest correlation/relative stability, not rank correlation or absolute agreement; no coefficient interval extracted.
records.repeated_session: Two assessment visits; model-specific paired n unverified.
records.invariance: Treatment, longitudinal scalar and context invariance unestablished.
records.temporal_order: Retrospective global ratings; no tic-level lead-lag test.
records.clustering: Participant-level scores; shared CBIT cohort, not independent efficacy evidence.
records.missingness: Endpoint-specific complete-case counts and missing-item method unverified.
records.transfer_estimand: No randomized untrained-context or untrained-tic effect.
records.alternative_explanation: Stable reporting style or awareness can preserve rank despite a systematic shift.

records.title: The premonitory urge revisited: An individualized premonitory urge for tics scale
records.population: 75 clinic youth aged 6–17; I-PUTS available for 73.
records.construct: Clinician-rated past-week, tic-specific urge number, frequency and intensity.
records.comparator: Second-rater scoring of 15 randomly selected assessments.
records.reliability_type: Inter-rater ICC; model/agreement definition not verified.
records.repeated_session: No repeat-session stability demonstrated by these same-assessment ICCs.
records.invariance: Adult, treatment and context invariance unestablished.
records.clustering: 15 independent assessments for reliability; nested tics are not additional participants.
records.missingness: Two missing I-PUTS not imputed; other missing items addressed by expectation maximization under assumed MAR.
records.transfer_estimand: No intervention or reserved-tic transfer contrast.
records.alternative_explanation: Raters can agree on the same awareness-dependent report without calibrating latent generation.

records.title: Developing the Premonitory Urges for Tic Disorders Scale–Revised (PUTS-R)
records.population: Pooled 241 participants: 93 adults, 148 minors; three sites.
records.construct: PUTS item properties, severity/quality dimensions and proposed revised items.
records.comparator: Separate age-group classical/IRT and exploratory factor analyses.
records.result: Nine-item alpha=.83 in minors (n=137), .82 in adults (n=89). Item 2 loaded differently by age; items 1/9/10 had disordered thresholds; adult item 5 also problematic.
records.invariance: Similar factor count is not equal loadings/thresholds; new items still require validation.
records.clustering: Participant-level; pooled experiments may overlap earlier work; independence unverified.
records.missingness: 1% PUTS values missing, not replaced; analysis counts vary.
records.transfer_estimand: No intervention or cross-context causal transfer effect.
records.alternative_explanation: Age, language or interpretation can alter item functioning without changed generation.

records.title: Convergent Validity of the PUTS
records.population: 22 participants aged 17–55 for urge-monitor convergence; 40 youth for questionnaire factors.
records.construct: Global PUTS versus average continuous global urge rating.
records.comparator: Five-minute free-tic monitor task versus questionnaire.
records.result: PUTS9–monitor Pearson r=.66; PUTS10–monitor r=.64. Ten-item alpha=.79 in older sample, .84 in youth.
records.invariance: No treatment/context calibration; both urge measures are self-report.
records.temporal_order: 10-Hz monitor averaged after removing first ten seconds.
records.clustering: 2,900 retained readings condensed per participant; n=22, not 63,800 independent observations.
records.missingness: Sample-flow and full missingness not established.
records.transfer_estimand: No randomized transfer contrast; youth had no monitor validation here.
records.alternative_explanation: Shared awareness and reporting conventions generate convergence without an external latent anchor.

records.title: Urge-tic associations in children and adolescents with Tourette syndrome
records.population: 25 analyzed, aged 8–18; 11 additional acquired cases excluded; historical adult comparator n=21.
records.construct: Global momentary urge versus upper-body/video tic expression.
records.comparator: Concurrent five-minute series; historical age-group comparison.
records.result: Individual logistic associations: 11 positive, 12 nonsignificant, 2 negative. Rater Pearson r medians .71 (presence), .80 (intensity); not absolute agreement.
records.invariance: Age/context invariance not established by matched coding.
records.temporal_order: Concurrent association; anticipation and recording latency remain alternatives.
records.clustering: Seconds/tics nested within participants; individual analyses reported; exact serial-null implementation unverified.
records.missingness: 11 unusable: video8, urge acquisition2, task1. Eight analyzed participants lacked vocal audio. Non-vocal-only sensitivity minimally changed the age comparisons.
records.transfer_estimand: Historical age comparison is not intervention transfer.
records.alternative_explanation: Anticipation, lower-body omission or observation differences can alter association.

records.title: Effects of Tic Suppression and Urge Monitoring on Premonitory Urges and Tic Frequency in Tourette Syndrome
records.population: Collected 2012–2013: 14 referred, 11 eligible/consenting, one experimental exclusion, ten adult men analyzed; YGTSS≥20, frequent tics/urges, no prior behavioral therapy.
records.construct: Pressure-monitor urge reports, post-trial VAS urge/fatigue and video tic counts.
records.comparator: Four five-minute conditions twice; constrained randomized order; suppression includes reward.
records.result: Suppression minus suppression+reporting: urge VAS −11.2 [95% CI −21.7,−.8]; fatigue −12.2 [−22.7,−1.6]. Mean-monitor reporting minus suppression+reporting −.02 [−.13,.10]. Tic-reporting contrasts nonsignificant.
records.reliability_type: Manipulation contrast; no session absolute-agreement estimate.
records.repeated_session: Two within-session trials per condition; paired comparisons df=9. One event-trajectory trial has eight contributors because two had no qualifying episodes.
records.invariance: Pressure references are within-person subjective calibration, not an external anchor; exploratory p-values unadjusted.
records.temporal_order: Real-time measures and post-trial recall differ.
records.clustering: Paired participant comparisons, n=10; repeated trials not independent people.
records.missingness: Recruitment/analysis flow verified in subsequent main-text review; event trajectories have outcome-specific denominators.
records.transfer_estimand: Laboratory reporting/suppression contrast; no untreated-context durability/function estimand.
records.alternative_explanation: Attention, device workload, genuine sensation and report criteria remain entangled.
